newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: McRetail lifts profile with Botswana float.
newsitem.headline: McRetail lifts profile with Botswana float.

text.p: South African retailer McCarthy Retail listed 160.05 million of its shares on the Botswana Stock Exchange (BSE) on Tuesday in a move to boost the group's profile in the country.
"We want to enhance investor and public awareness of our company," McRetail Botswana chairman Frank Lukin said.
The company is already listed on the Johannesburg Stock Echange (JSE).
Over the coming year, the group plans to open 15 new outlets in Botswana. Bonus Building Supplies would grow from a two to a 10 store network and Beares would open seven new stores.
Botswana vice-president and Minister of Finance and Development Planning Festus Mogae welcomed the listing as a milestone in the development of the capital market in Botswana.
"Such listings will greatly enhance domestic investment opportunities," Mogae said.

The dual listing, the third on the BSE this year, is expected to add 1.85 billion pula or four percent to the exchange's market capitalisation, taking total market capitalisation to 52.3 billion pula.
McRetail shares closed on the JSE at 14.50 rand on Monday.
"I hope that the McCarthy group will be able to find and develop sources of supply in Botswana," Mogae added. The group is already looking at a facility to manufacture furniture in Botswana.

Mogae said the Botswana government was committed to promoting the growth of retail business by removing all barriers for entry to the sector. The Trade and Liquor Act had been amended to remove all impediments that might negatively influence investmen.
"We will continue to knock down barriers to investment on all fronts in order to create room for a dynamic private sector," he said.
"Private foreign investment is an essential ingredient of our economic development. Domestic savings and investment are in short supply."
Botswana needed the management talent and technology that normally accompanied such investments.
McRetail's investments in Botswana are its largest out of South Africa. The group's total investment in Botswana is 60 million pula.

In November 1996, the group bought control of the Botswana Land Rover dealership, BM Engineering (BME) for 10 million pula cash, adding it to a 50 million pula investment in retail stores Game, Beares, Savells, Bee Gee, Prefsure, Guys 'n Girls, Happy Homes and Bonus Building Supplies.
